# Create new work

This entry holds the route and tells you which shared modules to load. Fetch each module as raw text from `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aispanda/Reusable-Delivery/<SHA>/modules/<file>` using the same pinned SHA as this entry. When several triggers apply, load every listed module before the action. Load each once per task at that SHA and reuse its verified contents while available.

Track the route, SHA, modules loaded, current step, results, blockers and next action in the story's linked execution record, or in the story while no separate record is needed. Read and update the current revision of that record, not a pinned copy linked from the story. For each required `modules/<file>`, verify the pinned SHA and its matching final marker: `<!-- end of modules/<file> -->`. On resumption, reuse verified content still available. Reload only the triggered material whose contents or provenance are missing. If a module cannot be verified, hold the dependent action and use the selected route’s full guide at the same SHA. Record the fallback in the current progress record. The [NEW](../new/DELIVERY.md) and [MIGRATE](../migrate/DELIVERY.md) full guides end with “Supporting detail when needed” and its validation-history sentence. Separately required files, including CODE-QUALITY.md when triggered, still need to be available at that SHA. Keep dependent work blocked if required content remains unavailable.

Apply the selected route and every trigger for the current action. “Privacy, publication and links” maps to `privacy.md` and `publication.md`. “Executors and bounded execution” maps to `execution.md` and `states.md`, plus `automation.md` when its trigger applies. Load each module when its trigger applies and reuse verified content at the same SHA. On NEW, use `privacy.md` for criterion comparison in step 3 and `review.md` when planning verification in step 4. On MIGRATE, use `platform.md` before external inventory reads and `execution.md` and `states.md` before reconciling status or selecting Next. On either route, use `publication.md` before a commit, push, publication or ClickUp write. Read worked examples, model examples, archive, validation history and optional repository settings only when useful.

Use one guide commit: record a commit-pinned link's SHA; otherwise resolve the supplied branch/tag once and read this document at that SHA. Reuse content already fully present and verified at the same SHA; reread only if changed, truncated or provenance is uncertain. API clients must pass the SHA explicitly. Record this document path, SHA, route, any modules loaded and progress in the current revision of the progress record: the story's linked execution record, or the story while no separate record is needed. Refresh deliberately and reconcile changed rules; never mix revisions.

If required content is missing, inaccessible or incomplete, report it and stop dependent work; do not guess or silently substitute an older copy. Continue independent authorized work only when the gap cannot invalidate it. This guide grants no authority to build, deploy, spend, share externally or change criteria. A link supplies neither inaccessible chat history nor permission. Infer inputs and existing authority from available context; ask only for unresolved information needed for the next action.

## Route

1. Establish the beneficiary, outcome, scope, exclusions, known facts and open decisions from the request and relevant sources. Check for existing related work before creating a duplicate. If this is existing or partly existing work, switch to ../migrate/START.md at this same SHA before dependent writes.
2. Confirm the intended repository, folder, current branch, existing changes and authorization. Reuse an appropriate repository/folder; create a new repository only when authorized. Ask for a genuinely missing destination or decision rather than inventing one. No fixed artifact count is required.
3. Create `story.md` using the Copyable story template. Define observable criteria with stable IDs. Preserve requirements already agreed in the brief; label new interpretations as proposals. Apply the Privacy, publication and links rules for sanitization mapping and source/published criterion comparison. Keep unknown owners and results explicit. Link any design or research needed to execute the story.
4. Record one next eligible action. Keep its detailed execution contract in the linked record when needed. Apply the Executors and bounded execution and Review and acceptance rules.
5. Apply the Privacy, publication and links rules for publication checks. After GitHub readback, create/update the authorized ClickUp item with its short title/ID, applicable grouping/filtering fields and owner/date/status fields; set its description to the story's Outcome sentence, copied verbatim, and one direct link to the current GitHub story file. Apply the Privacy, publication and links rules for preservation and concurrency checks before replacing any existing ClickUp description. Verify the saved pointer and fields.
6. Continue eligible work already authorized, recording results using the Executors and bounded execution rules. Story creation alone is not permission to build or deploy. Report verified results, remaining decisions and the next action.
